homepage.description.message: Development documentation for XRobot and LibXR.

homepage.hero.lead.message: A modular framework for robotics development, device interfaces, and engineering automation. LibXR provides core semantics, driver abstractions, and XRUSB; the CodeGenerator generates LibXR peripheral code from STM32CubeMX projects; XRobot manages Modules and generates the main function XRobotMain.

homepage.guide.onboarding.desc.message: Pick the right starting path by platform, then get familiar with XR design ideas and the basic coding style step by step.

homepage.guide.agent.desc.message: A one-page startup context for a dedicated XRobot / LibXR assistant: identify the repository role first, then jump into the right docs and code entry points.

homepage.panel.title.message: Jump straight into the docs from the task at hand

homepage.route.xrobot.desc.message: Fetching and locking Modules, configurations, and main function generation.

homepage.route.core.desc.message: Callbacks, events, messages, time, memory, and the foundational abstractions.

homepage.route.driver.desc.message: Peripheral abstractions, platform implementations, and XRUSB as part of the driver layer.

homepage.route.start.desc.message: Platform selection, tool installation, and environment setup.

homepage.quick.desc.message: Documentation entry points by common task.

homepage.path.intro.title.message: I am new to LibXR / XRobot

homepage.path.intro.desc.message: Start with the overall concepts, repository structure, and the smallest working path before deciding which layer to dive into.

homepage.path.core.title.message: I want to port to a new hardware platform

homepage.path.core.desc.message: Start from driver abstractions, platform implementation, and basic peripheral capabilities to understand the board-level foundation first.

homepage.path.driver.title.message: I need to work on device-side interfaces and links

homepage.path.driver.desc.message: Start from device interfaces, protocol stacks, and transport implementations, then look at communication, identification, and update-related content.

homepage.path.usb.title.message: I want to get the project running quickly

homepage.path.usb.desc.message: First tell an XRobot BSP from a LibXR-only project; the Agent prompt on this page can classify the project.

homepage.recent.desc.message: Development directions that have recently started or are in progress.

homepage.recent.core.title.message: Platform drivers cover STM32, CH32, ESP32, HPM, MSPM0, Linux, Webots, and WebAssembly

homepage.recent.core.desc.message: Each platform's drivers live in their own subdirectory under driver/ in LibXR.

homepage.recent.linux.title.message: XRUSB already covers CDC, DAP, DFU, GSUSB, HID, and UAC

homepage.recent.linux.desc.message: XRUSB provides several USB device classes, each documented on its own page.

homepage.recent.usb.title.message: The debug path supports SWD and JTAG, with the implementation split into layers

homepage.recent.usb.desc.message: The debug implementation covers GPIO-timed SWD and JTAG and the CMSIS-DAP v1/v2 device classes.

homepage.focus.desc.message: Common questions fall into three groups: runtime mechanisms, hardware integration, and project builds.

homepage.focus.core.desc.message: How callbacks, events, messages, and middleware relate.

homepage.focus.driver.desc.message: Drivers, platform implementations, XRUSB, and debug links.

homepage.focus.project.desc.message: Let the Agent identify the repository type first, then choose the workspace, platform-project, or driver entry path so the initialization flow starts from the right place.

homepage.foot.desc.message: Project background, how to contribute, and community entry points.
